tool_input.command:
/opt/homebrew/bin/Rscript -e '
set.seed(1)
X <- cbind(1, rnorm(4), rnorm(4), c(1,0,0,0), c(0,1,0,0), c(0,0,1,0), c(0,0,0,1))
colnames(X) <- c("(Intercept)","a","b","IND_1","IND_2","IND_3","IND_4")
y <- rnorm(4)
f <- lm.wfit(X, y, rep(1,4)); print(f$coefficients); print(f$rank)
# constant column later than intercept
X2 <- cbind(1, rnorm(10), 1, rnorm(10)); colnames(X2) <- c("(Intercept)","a","GRIEV","b")
print(lm.wfit(X2, rnorm(10), rep(1,10))$coefficients)
# n=0
r <- try(lm.wfit(X[0,,drop=FALSE], y[0], numeric(0))); print(class(r))
'
tool_input.description: Check lm.wfit aliasing behaviour with n < p and constant columns

result:
The repair round is complete. All deliverables are in `code/`.

**What changed in the code** (`code/k7_lib.R`, `code/run_grid.R`):

- **A1 HC3.** Rows with hat value at or above 1 minus 1e-8 now contribute exactly zero to the HC3 meat, for original fits, restricted refits and deletion refits, with the weighted design under WLS. A new last column `n_leverage_one` was added to model_stats.csv. On the synthetic file every fitted model has such rows, and the old code produced 0/0 there.
- **A5 column handling.** Only industry dummies can be dropped. Any other all-zero or collinear term fails the model with that reason, never a reduced model. Industry collinearity is resolved before the residual-df check. Nested tests enforce a numerator df of 6 or 3 and fail with a reason otherwise.
- **A6 / A10 failure records.** Dropped-column info survives a failed fit. A failed original influence model yields one failed row per estimation-sample record. Nested-test failures and every failed deletion are listed in run_info.json with reasons. nested_tests.csv gained trailing `status` and `error` columns.
- **A7 copy validity.** Level-specific exclusions are applied to the raw items before the copy, so an invalid CORE item (0 or 995 under staff L0, declared codes, out-of-range ILM/INCENT codes) never triggers the system-missing copy, never overwrites a valid GSS item, and the manager fallback uses the GSS item.
- **A8 reference sample.** Family samples are determined once from item validity flags before any standardization and are never recomputed.
- **A2, A4, A9.** Spec-level top codes are read with the code kept before declared-missing handling. V8, V17 and V43 pass through metadata missing codes. SUBSID L1/L2 is missing when V17 is system-missing. Staff code 996 is explicitly missing.

**Checker items left unchanged, with reasons in the README:** item 3 (A4 confirms SUBSID missing on system-missing V17), item 10 (A6 permits null in JSON), item 11 (A3 confirms log10 of the recoded count).

**Verification**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Tests | 263 passed, 0 failed (`code/dev_out/test_results.txt`) |
| Grid run | 38 specs into `code/dev_out/v1_1/`, 888 of 912 models ok |
| Failures | 24 models and 8 nested tests of D05 only, empty sample on the permuted file, all with recorded reasons |
| HC3 | no non-finite values in any coefficient row |

New tests cover HC3 with a leverage-one row for OLS and WLS against the explicit zeroed formula, the copy-rule validity rule at all three staff_coding levels including the manager fallback, industry-only drops and failure reasons, per-record failed influence rows, and validity-based samples. The README has the "v1.1 changes" section listing every amendment and checker item, and `code/DONE_v1_1.txt` is written.
